excludes: Creative image generation/editing is owned by native imagegen.
Browser image optimization is owned by image-optimization.
Adaptive playback is owned by video-streaming.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement untrusted image/document/audio/video ingestion, isolated processing, extraction/moderation, provider-cap enforcement, metadata/PII governance, storage and delivery.

risk.rationale: multimodal-processing can change production data, model, media, security, retrieval or financial behavior and requires explicit scope, rollback and affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Optimize responsive webpage image markup, framework loaders, LCP priority, CDN caching and remote optimizer security.
Implement adaptive video playback manifests, player buffering, DRM/captions and streaming delivery rather than media ingestion/extraction.

positive.prompt: Implement a tenant media ingestion pipeline that verifies signatures, quarantines uploads, bounds decoder/transcoder resources, strips governed metadata/PII, records provenance and authorizes every derivative.

Add OCR/transcription/vision processing using installed provider capability and current caps, queued idempotent state, moderation, partial failure and deletion across source/intermediates/derivatives.

assertions.criterion: Implements untrusted media-to-data ingestion and processing without implementing or claiming ownership of creative generation, web image delivery or adaptive playback.
Inspects source trust, formats/signatures, metadata/PII classes, storage/queues/processors, provider pins/caps, consumers, auth, rights and retention from the fixture.
Defines canonical identity/state/provenance and accepted capability, resource/isolation/provider bounds, moderation/quarantine and derivative authorization before processing.

Rejects spoofed media, isolates and bounds decompression/pixel/frame/document work, minimizes governed metadata/PII, enforces current installed provider caps before upload and links authorized derivatives/retention/deletion idempotently.

Tests malformed/polyglot/bomb media, malicious metadata, PII leakage, provider-cap rejection, duplicate/replay, partial upload/crash, moderation failure, cross-tenant derivative access and complete deletion.
Reports media/trust/rights contracts, state/resources/provider capability, metadata/PII policy, storage/retention, fixtures/quality evidence and residual decoder/provider risk.
Keeps provider cap/model/format matrices out of source, uses versioned processor adapters and centralizes derivative provenance/lifecycle.

scenarios.prompt: A multimodal endpoint trusts MIME/extension, decodes user video/images in the app process, preserves EXIF/GPS and document metadata, uploads oversized inputs directly to a provider and stores OCR/transcripts without tenant authorization or deletion linkage. Repair it.

assertions.criterion: Rejects or quarantines before unsafe decode, derives tenant server-side, enforces bounded isolated processing and stops provider transfer until retention/data-processing authority is verified.
Detects decompression/pixel bomb behavior, strips or governs metadata/PII, prevents cross-tenant access and records consent/rights/provenance for any provider processing.
Requires resource-limit evidence, no metadata/PII leakage, tenant isolation, provider deletion/retention evidence and cleanup of partial/intermediate artifacts.

scenarios.prompt: A customer uploads a tiny compressed image that expands beyond available memory and contains GPS/identity metadata; an OCR provider may retain input and the requested tenant is client-supplied.

assertions.criterion: Uses the skill-required repository stack-context step when execution is available, then derives authority from the lockfile/installed types and matching official provider docs to resolve supported modalities/formats/caps and rejects unsupported input before upload. When execution is withheld, stating that required stack-context generation and underlying evidence are unavailable is sufficient without literal shell syntax, but it must not claim the step ran.
Checks SDK/model capability, runtime decoder/transcoder, queue/storage limits, provider region/retention and consumer schema together.
Stores verified capability in adapter/configuration and tests rather than remembered model names, quotas or format tables in the skill.

scenarios.prompt: The installed provider SDK supports fewer media formats and lower request caps than current examples. The pipeline change cannot upgrade it.
